purpose: Defines what an implementation strategy document is and the principles for writing it, especially for additive development, as a generic fallback when no project rules exist.
summary: Definition of the implementation strategy document: responsibility, dependency on design, lifecycle
Relationship to the next stage: the plan document is built on the strategy
What the strategy document does not write: structural design and individual task units
Boundary with the plan document: phase-order units versus task executability units
Why additive development is the hardest case: conflicting, new, and subtly changed items
Do not bind decisions with procedures; avoid inertia toward patching; follow design
Target of strategy is existing implementation code, not old-spec documents
Constraints received from the additive development spec sections
tasks: Deciding how to modify, delete, merge, or split existing code
title: 実装戦略書 作成原則
